text.p: Dubai government-owned Emirates airline said on Monday it was buying 16 A330-200 aircraft from the European consortium Airbus Industrie.
It has an optoin for to buy a further seven aircraft, Emirates chairman Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed al-Maktoum told a news conference.
"The new aircraft will gradually replace the present airbuses from January 1999 until the year 2002," Sheikh Ahmed said.
Emirates fleet includes 16 Airbus A310 and A300s. It recently took delivery of its third Boeing aircraft 777. It has another four 777s on firm order and an option for seven more.
Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Germany's Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
